site.aboutHeading: On light, and waiting for it.
site.aboutText:
I've come to think of a camera as a slow instrument, even when the shutter is fast. Most of what happens before a photograph is made is attention — to a room, a coastline, a face — long enough that whatever is true about it has a chance to appear on its own terms.

I work across three subjects that don't, on the surface, have much in common: people, landscapes, and cars. What connects them is a working method rather than a style — I try to arrive early, stay longer than seems necessary, and photograph only once the obvious version of the scene has passed.

I'm not especially interested in decisive moments. I'm interested in the ordinary minutes on either side of them, which is usually where the actual subject is standing.
site.printsIntro:
A number of photographs from each collection are available as archival fine-art prints, produced in small runs through a dedicated print partner. Paper, sizing, and framing are handled entirely on their side — I'm involved only in approving the print itself before it leaves the studio.

Not every image is available as a print. Where one is, you'll find a "View Print Options" link on that photograph's page, which will take you to the print partner's site to review formats and place an order.
site.printsNote: Ordering, framing, and shipping are handled entirely by the external print partner. This site exists to show the work — not to process print orders directly.
